name: 46,XX Difference of Sex Development Induced by Fetal Androgens Excess
aliases: 46,XX DSD due to Fetal Androgen Excess
46,XX Disorder of Sex Development with Prenatal Androgen Exposure

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for 46,XX DSD due to Fetal Androgen Excess

criteria.description: Presence of ambiguous external genitalia at birth in a 46,XX individual
Elevated serum or urinary androgen levels consistent with fetal androgen excess
Confirmed 46,XX chromosomal complement without Y chromosome material
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in steroidogenesis (e.g., CYP21A2, CYP11B1)
Imaging showing presence of uterus and ovaries consistent with female internal genitalia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ambiguous genitalia in a 46,XX individual combined with elevated androgen levels and confirmed 46,XX karyotype
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing and hormonal assays are critical for confirming diagnosis and differentiating from other DSD etiologies.

pathognomonic.notes: Enlarged clitoris due to prenatal androgen exposure
Partial or complete fusion of labioscrotal folds mimicking scrotum
Degree of virilization classified by Prader scale

common.notes: Excessive hair growth in androgen-sensitive areas
Accelerated skeletal maturation due to androgen excess

common.symptomName: Uterus and ovaries present on pelvic ultrasound
searchTerms: normal uterus and ovaries on ultrasound
female reproductive organs seen on scan
pelvic ultrasound shows uterus and ovaries

occasional.notes: Electrolyte imbalance due to aldosterone deficiency in some enzyme defects
Abnormal urethral meatus position due to virilization
searchTerms: urethra opening on underside of penis

occasional.symptomName: Psychosocial distress related to ambiguous genitalia
occasional.notes: Emotional and social challenges in affected individuals
searchTerms: mental health issues due to genital ambiguity

rare.notes: Elevated blood pressure due to mineralocorticoid excess
searchTerms: high blood pressure from enzyme deficiency
blood pressure raised by 11-beta hydroxylase problem

rare.notes: Functional cysts due to hormonal imbalance

imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing presence of uterus and ovaries
Bone age assessment indicating advanced skeletal maturation
genetic: Pathogenic variants in CYP21A2, CYP11B1, or other steroidogenic enzyme genes
Normal 46,XX karyotype confirmed by chromosomal analysis
other: Prader scale assessment of genital ambiguity
Clinical evaluation of external genitalia morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Female external genitalia with absent uterus
Elevated serum testosterone with androgen receptor defects
Presence of both ovarian and testicular tissue

redFlags: Severe ambiguous genitalia requiring urgent evaluation
Salt-wasting crisis with dehydration and electrolyte imbalance
Adrenal crisis presenting with hypotension and shock
